input_signals.name: Improving Profits With Earned Capital
input_signals.hypothesis: An upward trend in operating profitability is credible when the firm has a deep stock of retained earnings, since cumulative internally generated capital verifies that past profits were real and reinvestable rather than one-time or externally financed.
input_signals.reasoning: TREND captures the profitability-improvement channel while retained earnings over assets is a balance-sheet quality/maturity measure of accumulated earnings history, so the pair distinguishes a genuine profitability ramp from a fragile turnaround at a capital-depleted firm. Neither leg alone contains this validation logic: young cash-burning firms can trend upward from a very low base, and mature high-RE firms can be stagnant. The rank combination keeps both channels on a comparable scale and preserves broad coverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( trend( ratio( oiadp, at ), 5 ), ratio( re, at ) )

input_signals.name: Profits Not Propped By New Debt
input_signals.hypothesis: Sustained operating profitability accompanied by shrinking or flat debt reflects genuine internal cash generation, while equally high reported profitability alongside rapid new borrowing signals profits being financed and flattered by balance-sheet expansion that will reverse.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a flow rather than a level mechanism: it conditions the profitability state on the direction of debt financing over the past year, so it separates self-funding operators from firms whose apparent strength coincides with creditor support. The three-year moving average removes single-year profit noise without imposing the coverage cost of a five-year window. It tests a financing-flow channel that neither gen-0 survivor examined.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ma( ratio( oiadp, at ), 3 ) ), rank( neg( growth( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Working Capital Backed Profitability
input_signals.hypothesis: High operating profitability is more likely to persist when the firm holds enough net working capital relative to its total obligations to fund the operating cycle internally, since liquidity-constrained profitable firms must divert operating cash to near-term claims rather than to shareholders.
input_signals.reasoning: This is the graded repair of the gen-0 binary solvency gate: net working capital scaled by total liabilities enters as a continuous rank, so firms are ordered smoothly by liquidity instead of being dumped en masse into the short leg, which prevents the spread from degenerating into a pure distress bet. Both legs use high-coverage annual items and no time window at all, so it should have the broadest coverage in this batch. It isolates the liquidity channel of financial health, separate from the debt-level channel in Signal 1.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( act, lct ), lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Rollover Risk Adjusted Profitability
input_signals.hypothesis: What makes profitability fragile is not the amount of debt but its maturity: a profitable firm whose claims are concentrated in debt due within a year must keep refinancing at the mercy of credit markets, so its operating strength is hostage to rollover conditions, while the same profitability financed with long-dated or non-debt claims is insulated.
input_signals.reasoning: The quality leg is the short-term share of the liability structure, which is orthogonal by construction to the leverage level used in Quality-Minus-Junk safety, so this tests maturity composition rather than rediscovering profitability-plus-low-leverage. The interaction is the point: refinancing risk should erode the value of high operating profitability far more than it matters for firms with little profit to protect, and the rank product concentrates the long leg on profitable firms with term-funded balance sheets. Scaling short-term debt by total liabilities rather than assets keeps the measure defined for debt-free firms and avoids simply re-expressing total leverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), rank( neg( ratio( dlc, lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Profit Coverage Of Near Term Claims
input_signals.hypothesis: The relevant measure of durable operating strength is how many times current-year operating profit covers the claims coming due within the year; a firm whose annual EBITDA dwarfs its current liabilities is structurally insulated, while an equally profitable firm whose near-term claims exceed its profit stream is one bad year from creditor control.
input_signals.reasoning: The two archive winners both scale a claim measure by total liabilities and then rank-multiply with profitability; this proposal collapses the same economics into a single credit-style coverage ratio, which lets us learn whether the payoff comes from the interaction structure or simply from measuring profit relative to imminent obligations. Industry adjustment is essential because current-liability intensity is highly sector-dependent (retail and utilities versus software), so the raw ratio would otherwise sort industries rather than firms. Both inputs are among the best-populated annual items, so coverage should be at the high end of the archive.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_adj( ratio( oibdp, lct ) )

input_signals.name: Funding Pressure Adjusted Profitability
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt), NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Liquidity buffers and debt-maturity structure are two separable dimensions of near-term funding pressure, and profitability is most durable when both are favourable: liquid resources cover the operating cycle *and* little of the liability stack must be refinanced immediately.
input_signals.reasoning: This directly tests whether the two independently successful quality legs are complementary or redundant — if the combined score beats both parents on alpha and t-statistic, funding pressure is genuinely multi-dimensional; if it merely matches them, the legs are proxies for one another and later generations should stop adding balance-sheet channels. The inner SUMRANK equalises the weight of the liquidity and maturity legs before they gate profitability, avoiding the silent double-weighting problem flagged earlier. Coverage should match the parents since all four inputs are standard balance-sheet items.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), rank( sumrank( ratio( sub( act, lct ), lt ), neg( ratio( dlc, lt ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Profits Without Payables Stretch
input_signals.hypothesis: A profitable firm that is quietly financing itself by letting current liabilities outrun its sales base is converting supplier and accrual credit into reported operating strength; that funding source is finite and reversible, so such profitability is less durable than profitability generated with a stable trade-credit position.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a different failure mode from the interest-bearing debt-growth flow that produced negative alpha in gen 1 — trade credit and accrued obligations are not capital-market financing, and stretching them is a documented precursor of operating strain rather than a deliberate leverage decision. Benchmarking current-liability growth against contemporaneous sales growth removes the mechanical scaling that made the raw debt-growth leg behave like a size-and-investment tilt. It gives the batch one genuine flow mechanism to sit alongside the level-based consolidation, so we learn whether *any* flow variable can work in this theme pair or whether only levels do.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), rank( neg( sub( growth( lct, 1 ), growth( sale, 1 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Habitually Liquid Profitable Firms
input_signals.hypothesis: A liquidity buffer is a policy, not an accident: firms that have maintained positive net working capital in every one of the last five years have demonstrated an institutionalised commitment to self-funding their operating cycle, and their current profitability is therefore far more likely to survive a demand or credit shock than the profitability of a firm that only happens to be liquid this year.
input_signals.reasoning: This is not smoothing — it replaces the magnitude of the balance-sheet leg with a count of how many years the solvency condition actually held, which is a track-record concept that no moving average can express and which the two failed MA signals therefore did not test. The count is coarse and outlier-immune, so unlike the level-based liquidity leg it cannot be driven by a handful of cash-hoarding observations, and ranking it before multiplication keeps both legs bounded with no zero-crossing pathology. It also tells us something decision-relevant: whether the archive's liquidity payoff comes from the current buffer size or from a persistent financial policy.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), rank( ts_sum( indicator( sub( act, lct ), 0 ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Trough Profit Cover Of Current Claims
input_signals.hypothesis: Financial durability should be assessed under stress: the right question is not whether this year's profit covers claims coming due, but whether the firm's *worst* operating profit of the recent past would still have covered them, since that is the state in which creditors force asset sales or dilutive financing.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces a functional-form tweak with a genuinely new economic object — a self-referential stress test that crosses the firm's own historical downside in operating profit with the size of its near-term obligations — and it is not a monotone transform of any archive signal because two firms with identical current coverage can differ sharply in their trough coverage. Industry adjustment is necessary because both the cyclicality of EBITDA and the intensity of current liabilities are sector traits, so the raw ratio would sort industries rather than firms. Using a minimum rather than a mean or standard deviation keeps the emphasis on downside survivability, which is the part of stability that creditors and equity holders actually care about.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: ind_adj( ratio( ts_min( oibdp, 5 ), lct ) )

input_signals.name: Rollover Need Versus Liquid Resources
input_signals.hypothesis: Refinancing risk is not about how much of the liability stack is short-dated but about whether liquid resources already on hand can retire the maturing debt; a profitable firm whose current assets far exceed its short-term debt faces no rollover decision at all, whereas one with the same maturity mix but thin liquid assets must return to lenders on their terms.
input_signals.reasoning: This changes the economics of the winning leg rather than its form: dlc/lt measures the composition of claims, while dlc/act measures whether the firm can self-retire those claims, which is the mechanism the rollover story actually invokes. It also unifies the two independently successful quality legs (liquidity and maturity) into a single asset-versus-obligation comparison instead of blending their ranks, which is a substantively different aggregation from gen-2's SUMRANK merge. Both inputs are dense, so coverage should be at the top of the archive range.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), rank( neg( ratio( dlc, act ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Within Industry Profit And Maturity
input_signals.hypothesis: Both operating profitability and reliance on short-term debt are heavily sector-determined, so the priced information should be a firm's standing relative to its industry peers rather than its position in the pooled cross-section; industry-neutral scoring should raise abnormal returns by stripping out sector bets that FF5 factors partly absorb.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a conditioning-set experiment on the best archive signal, not a formula tweak: pooled ranks let capital-intensive, short-debt-heavy industries populate the short leg wholesale, which produces industry rather than firm selection and can inflate factor loadings while diluting alpha. Industry-relative ranking preserves the exact economic interaction while enforcing peer comparability, and the earlier IND_ADJ result is uninformative here because that signal also abandoned the rank-product structure. A clear improvement would tell later generations to industry-neutralise both legs by default.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( dlc, lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Profit Volatility Against Obligations
input_signals.hypothesis: Fragility arises when the variability of the profit stream is large relative to the obligations that must be paid regardless of business conditions; a firm whose EBITDA fluctuates by a small fraction of its current liabilities can always service them, while equal profitability with fluctuations comparable to its near-term claims implies a real probability of a funding shortfall.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive's volatility failure used the volatility of the capital structure itself, which is a financing-policy artefact; here the second moment is applied to the profit stream and is scaled by the obligations it must cover, making it a crude distance-to-distress rather than a stability anomaly. This is the only construction in the batch in which the two themes interact inside a single quantity, and it tests whether cash-flow risk relative to claims adds anything beyond the static claim structure. The five-year window is affordable given that comparable windows have cost the archive little coverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), rank( neg( ratio( vol( oibdp, 5 ), lct ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Rising Short Debt Reliance Penalty
input_signals.hypothesis: A profitable firm that is actively shifting its funding toward short-dated debt is revealing either loss of access to term credit or a deliberate bet on refinancing conditions, and that migration predicts deterioration in the durability of its profits even before the level of short-term debt looks alarming.
input_signals.reasoning: Flow constructions have failed twice, but both used aggregate debt or trade-credit growth, which are contaminated by investment and size effects; this applies the change operator to the *specific ratio* that has produced the archive's most reliable alpha, so a null result cleanly establishes that this channel is a level effect and closes off flow variants for good. If instead it works, it identifies a faster-moving, higher-turnover version of the winning mechanism with distinct timing. The construction is bounded, uses only dense items, and requires a single lag.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), rank( neg( delta( ratio( dlc, lt ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Repeated Debt Service Capacity
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm demonstrates durable financial strength when its annual operating profit has repeatedly been large enough to retire the debt actually falling due, because that history shows it has never needed capital markets to survive its own maturity schedule; the level of profit relative to total claims then refines how much cushion that self-sufficiency carries.
input_signals.reasoning: The counted bar is now operating profit against maturing debt rather than against all current liabilities, which is a threshold a large part of the cross-section clears in some years and fails in others, so the count spreads across its full zero-to-five range instead of collapsing to zero for most firms. The second channel is a smoothed profit-to-total-liabilities coverage level, a quantity not present in the archive, and it supplies continuous variation that breaks the ties inherent in a coarse count, giving stable rather than lumpy portfolio buckets. Neither channel is a previously evaluated signal, so this is a new persistence-plus-cushion construct rather than a splice of two archive entries.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ts_sum( indicator( sub( oibdp, dlc ), 0 ), 5 ), ma( ratio( oibdp, lt ), 3 ) )

input_signals.name: Never Rollover Dependent Profits
input_signals.hypothesis: A single clean year of low short-term debt says little, because firms can temporarily term out debt before reporting; what identifies genuine funding independence is never having leaned on short-dated debt across a full business cycle, so profits earned by a firm whose worst rollover exposure in five years was still low are the most durable.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a worst-case rather than an average operator, so it is not the moving-average smoothing that failed twice in the archive; it asks whether the firm ever entered a state of refinancing dependence, which is the state in which profitable firms are forced into distressed choices. Because the persistence-count construction produced the archive's best Sharpe, there is direct evidence that multi-year conditions on the balance-sheet leg stabilise portfolio composition, and this applies that lesson to the single most reliable quality leg. Ranking keeps the leg bounded, so a handful of crisis-year spikes cannot dominate.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), rank( neg( ts_max( ratio( dlc, lt ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Self Retiring And Habitually Liquid
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, act)), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(SUB(act, lct), 0), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Funding independence has a level dimension and a history dimension: whether liquid assets on hand can retire maturing debt today, and whether the firm has kept its operating cycle self-funded year after year; profitability protected on both dimensions should be the most durable of all.
input_signals.reasoning: The two quality legs being merged were the archive's best on alpha (dlc/act, 3.7%) and on Sharpe (five-year solvency count, 0.332), and they are conceptually near-orthogonal because one is a current stock comparison and the other is a policy track record. Equal-weighting them by SUMRANK before the interaction avoids the double-weighting problem while testing whether level and persistence information are additive, which is the key open question for the consolidation phase. If alpha and Sharpe both exceed the parents, later generations should standardise on this composite quality leg.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), rank( sumrank( neg( ratio( dlc, act ) ), ts_sum( indicator( sub( act, lct ), 0 ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Peer Relative Margin And Liquidity
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating margins are almost entirely determined by industry technology, so a margin is informative about competitive advantage only relative to direct peers; a firm out-earning its industry on margin while holding enough liquid assets to retire its maturing debt is the clearest case of durable, self-funded operating strength.
input_signals.reasoning: The margin-based signal produced a large alpha but a weak Fama-MacBeth slope and near-zero Sharpe, the classic signature of a pooled sort that is really selecting industries, and industry-neutral ranking is the targeted fix for exactly that pathology rather than a generic wrapper. Pairing it with the self-retirement liquidity leg — also sector-dependent and therefore also industry-ranked — keeps the interaction intact while removing sector bets that FF5 partially absorbs. If the slope rises toward the level of the asset-scaled signals while alpha holds near 4%, the margin channel is salvageable and becomes a strong consolidation candidate.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, sale ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( dlc, act ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Profitability Plus Safe Firm Premium
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), MUL(RATIO(oibdp, at), INDICATOR(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt)), -0.1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Profitability is priced everywhere, but an extra premium accrues to profits earned by firms that owe almost nothing within the year, because for those firms the profit stream accrues to shareholders rather than being contingent on creditors renewing their claims; the correct specification therefore keeps the profitability main effect and adds a steeper slope inside the funding-safe group.
input_signals.reasoning: Every archive signal has used a pure rank product, which discards the profitability main effect and equalises the weight of the two legs by construction — a plausible reason the strongest alphas coincide with only moderate Fama-MacBeth slopes; this main-effect-plus-interaction form is a structurally new specification for this archive rather than an average of tested signals. The first channel preserves the full profitability ordering across all firms, while the second adds credit that scales with profitability only where short-term debt is under ten percent of liabilities, so the interaction steepens the profitability slope exactly where the economic story says it should. Inputs are dense, no time window is required, and the threshold is a genuine economic cutoff rather than a fitted parameter.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( oibdp, at ), mul( ratio( oibdp, at ), indicator( neg( ratio( dlc, lt ) ), -0.1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Hard Claims Versus Soft Claims
input_signals.hypothesis: Holding the total size of the liability stack fixed, financial debt is a hard, contractually enforceable claim that can force liquidation, while payables, accruals and deferred items are soft claims that renew automatically with the business; profitability supported mainly by soft claims is therefore far more durable than identical profitability pledged against hard debt.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a composition measure, not a leverage level: it is invariant to how large total liabilities are relative to assets, so it does not reproduce the profitability-plus-low-leverage quality composite the critic identified, and neither leg reuses the other's numerator so profitability is not double-counted. It also generalises the archive's most reliable finding — that the *type* of claim matters more than its quantity — from the maturity dimension to the enforceability dimension, which is a distinct and untested axis. All four inputs are among the densest annual items, so coverage should sit at the top of the archive range.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), rank( neg( ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Maturity Mismatch Penalty
input_signals.hypothesis: The classic funding pathology is financing illiquid, long-lived assets with debt that matures within a year; profitability generated on a mismatched balance sheet is fragile because the assets cannot be sold to meet the maturities, while the same profitability with maturities matched to liquid assets is safe.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive has compared short-term debt to total liabilities and to current assets, but never to the illiquid asset base it is actually funding, which is the specific comparison that defines maturity mismatch in banking and corporate finance. Because asset-light firms have small illiquid bases, the leg will assign them extreme values, but the rank transform bounds this and the economics are correct: short-dated debt against almost no fixed assets is genuinely precarious. It is a distinct hypothesis from claim composition, and its result will tell us whether the priced quantity is the liability mix or the asset-liability match.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), rank( neg( ratio( dlc, sub( at, act ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Earned Capital Against Total Claims
input_signals.hypothesis: Cumulative retained earnings relative to total obligations measures whether a firm's lifetime profits have already outgrown everything it owes; current profitability at such a firm is the latest instalment of a proven, creditor-independent earning history, whereas identical profitability at a firm whose claims dwarf its accumulated earnings is a first draw on an unproven franchise.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the near-term liquidity and maturity dimensions that the archive has now saturated and substitutes a long-horizon stock measure of solvency: the balance between lifetime earned capital and lifetime claims, which is conceptually orthogonal to whether this year's obligations happen to be short-dated. The two prior retained-earnings attempts scaled re by assets in an additive blend and used its one-year change as a payout proxy; neither compared it with the liability stack inside the multiplicative architecture that actually works in this archive. Both inputs are dense, no window is required, and negative retained earnings rank correctly at the bottom.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), rank( ratio( re, lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Pricing Power With Staying Power
input_signals.hypothesis: A wide margin is only defensible if the firm can afford to wait: holding inventory, extending customer credit and refusing discount demands all require working capital, so high-margin firms with deep liquidity can protect prices through a downturn while equally high-margin but illiquid firms must convert margin into cash by cutting prices.
input_signals.reasoning: The two legs have different denominators — revenue for the profit leg, total liabilities for the buffer leg — so unlike the flagged version this cannot collapse into a single coverage ratio, and it is not a monotone transform of any archived signal. It pairs the leg with the archive's largest alpha (margin, 3.9%) with the leg carrying the archive's best joint record (net working capital over liabilities: fmb 3.20, alpha 4.1%), a pairing never run because margin has only ever been crossed with debt-maturity legs. The economic content is specific: liquidity is what converts pricing power from an accounting fact into a defensible position.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oiadp, sale ) ), rank( ratio( sub( act, lct ), lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Self Liquidating Profit Premium
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), MUL(RATIO(oibdp, at), INDICATOR(SUB(oibdp, dlc), 0)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Profits carry an extra premium when a single year of operating income would retire every dollar of debt coming due, because such a firm can never be forced to the credit markets by its own maturity schedule; below that line profitability must be discounted for refinancing contingency.
input_signals.reasoning: The gate is now a clean, parameter-free comparison of the profit flow with maturing debt, which eliminates the dlc-inside-lct double counting the critic identified and makes the condition genuinely cross-theme rather than a rescaled version of the gen-4 cutoff. Retaining the profitability main effect in the first channel is the design feature that gave this specification full coverage, a 0.277 Sharpe and a preserved cross-sectional slope, which is exactly the joint-strength profile the objective asks for. Because dlc is small for many firms, the gate splits the cross-section broadly rather than degenerating to a rare condition.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( oibdp, at ), mul( ratio( oibdp, at ), indicator( sub( oibdp, dlc ), 0 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Rising Debt Service Coverage
input_signals.hypothesis: What matters for durability is the direction of the firm's solvency position: a profitable firm whose operating profit is growing relative to its total claims — whether by earning more or by retiring obligations — is converting operating success into financial resilience, while flat or deteriorating coverage signals that profits are being absorbed by the balance sheet.
input_signals.reasoning: Every flow construction that failed in this archive applied the change operator to a financing quantity alone (debt growth, payables growth), which is contaminated by investment and size; here the change is applied to the *joint* profit-to-claims ratio, so improvement can come from either side and the measure is scale-free. It is distinct from the profit-change leg because a firm can raise profitability while levering up, which this signal penalises and the pure profit change does not. Inputs are dense and only one lag is required.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), rank( delta( ratio( oibdp, lt ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Innovation Backed Profits Safely Funded
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Profitability is most persistent when it is defended by continuing investment in the product, and such investment is only sustainable if the firm is not exposed to refinancing pressure that forces discretionary spending cuts; profitable, research-intensive, term-funded firms should therefore have the most durable earning power.
input_signals.reasoning: R&D intensity is the one substantial theme resource the archive has never touched, and it supplies the economic mechanism — a defended competitive position — that the balance-sheet legs cannot express, so it is the batch's genuinely new channel rather than another recombination. Treating unreported R&D as zero is the standard and economically correct convention for firms that genuinely do no research, preserving full coverage instead of restricting the sample to reporters. If the moat channel adds nothing, the final generations can concentrate entirely on funding structure with a clear conscience.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( sumrank( ratio( oibdp, at ), ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ) ) ), rank( neg( ratio( dlc, lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Net Liquid Position After Debt
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, lct), dltt), lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The correct measure of financial protection is what remains of a firm's liquid resources once every financial claim, short and long, is deducted: a profitable firm whose current assets exceed both its current liabilities and its funded debt owes its future to no one, while the same profitability with a negative net position is a residual claim behind creditors.
input_signals.reasoning: This fuses into one economic quantity the two legs that have anchored opposite ends of the archive's performance — net working capital over liabilities (best alpha, 4.1%) and financial-debt share of claims (best slope, 3.31) — rather than averaging their ranks, so it tests whether a single net-financial-position measure dominates both parents on the joint criterion. Because liquid resources and funded debt enter with opposite signs in the same numerator, the measure is monotone in exactly the direction the economic story predicts and is scale-free after division by total liabilities. All inputs are dense and no window is required.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( sub( act, lct ), dltt ), lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Return On Financed Capital With Buffers
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, ADD(ADD(dltt, dlc), ceq))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The economically meaningful profitability rate is the return on capital that actually has to be serviced — funded debt plus shareholders' equity — rather than the return on a total asset base that is partly financed by free operating liabilities; a high return on financed capital held by a firm with deep working-capital buffers is the clearest evidence of a franchise that earns more than its cost of capital and can survive the cycle.
input_signals.reasoning: Every profitability leg in the archive has been scaled by assets or sales, so the invested-capital denominator is a genuinely new normalisation and not an average of tested signals: it mechanically rewards firms that generate profit while employing little financed capital, which is a different ordering from asset-scaled profitability whenever payables and accruals are large. Pairing it with the archive's best-performing quality leg keeps the comparison interpretable, and the two legs share no inputs, so the interaction is not double-counting. All inputs are dense annual items, so coverage should sit at the archive norm.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( oiadp, add( add( dltt, dlc ), ceq ) ) ), rank( ratio( sub( act, lct ), lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Working Capital Adjusted Cash Profit
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(oibdp, DELTA(SUB(act, lct), 1)), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Reported operating profit overstates durable earning power exactly when it is absorbed by a growing investment in receivables and inventory; subtracting the year's increase in net working capital yields the cash the operations actually threw off, and that cash-verified profitability is what determines whether a firm can meet claims without returning to creditors.
input_signals.reasoning: This delivers the cash-verification mechanism the flagged proposal was after while avoiding the coverage collapse the critic correctly identified, because the working-capital change is built from dense balance-sheet items rather than the sparse cash-flow statement item. input_signals.reasoning: Rather than stacking two tested R&D proxies on the profitability side, this puts research capital and total claims into a single scale-free quantity on the quality side, so the interaction being tested is the *financing source* of the intangible base rather than the timing of the debt that happens to sit against it. It is distinct from the archived knowledge-stock signal, which scaled the stock by assets and conditioned separately on short-term debt: here a firm with a large research base and heavy long-term obligations is penalised, which the parent does not do. Inputs are dense, the zero-fill convention remains economically correct for non-researchers, and the five-year window has cost this archive no coverage.
